comments.body: I reviewed Lucas's release-revision binding and Ben's two local cases. With the original approved release selected, authorization checks rev-approved. When changed contents become the release, rev-later-draft requires new approval. Policy Gates and audit remain in the path. I accepted the code review for deployment. Customer verification is still outstanding.

Megan's reviewed binding repair was deployed at 19:07 UTC. The approved-release and changed-release checks passed after deployment. This is a software deployment check. Hannah still needs Redpoint Assurance to try its original approved release before we call that customer case recovered.

Hannah received Ada's confirmation this morning that Publish completed for the original approved release after deployment. The later edited release is a separate approval request, tracked in CUSTO-10. Closing the original binding repair does not approve that changed content or settle Redpoint Assurance's wider account risk.

I extended the selector regression for the older Ashland proposal. ASH-KIT-P1 contains home-en, launch-en, launch-fr and pricing-en, with only launch-fr excluded. The selector returns home-en, launch-en and pricing-en. The excluded local variant stays out, and the other eligible consumers stay in. The case details are retained in the linked report.

I reviewed Sofia's patch and the additional ASH-KIT-P1 cases. The tested proposal now excludes its local launch variant and retains its eligible consumers. I accept this patch for that tested scope. A later proposal or variant still needs its own preview check before the customer can confirm it.

issues.description:
Redpoint Assurance's reviewer reopened a previously approved Change Set after a regional editor saved another draft. The sheet still showed the approved revision, but Publish was unavailable. The live site kept serving, with no report that the later draft went live.

Lucas compared the redacted Activity Log approval, Change Set, displayed revision and Honeycomb authorization request. On September 29, approval, Change Set and sheet all named rev-approved. Authorization instead tested rev-later-draft, which had not replaced the release revision. That located the first divergence in server revision selection and ruled out stale sheet presentation as the sole explanation.

Megan required the materially changed-release countercase before changing that binding. Lucas's September 30 local change produced:

| Change Set release revision | Local authorization result |
| --- | --- |
| Still rev-approved, with an unrelated newer draft saved | Existing named approval accepted |
| Changed to rev-later-draft | Renewed approval required |

Policy Gates and the audit path remained in authorization. Ben checked the corresponding local sheet and authorization states, and Lucas handed the change to Megan for review. The revision labels above are redacted case labels, not production revision IDs. At 17:20 UTC on September 30, code review and Redpoint Assurance's own verification were still open.

Megan accepted the code review at 18:12 UTC on September 30. Lucas deployed the reviewed binding repair at 19:07 UTC and checked both release cases afterward. The account had not yet verified its workflow at deployment time. On October 1, Hannah received Ada's confirmation that Publish completed for the original approved release still labeled rev-approved. This closes the original binding defect.

Ada's later edited release names changed contents, labeled rev-later-draft. Publish remains unavailable until that release receives new named approval. Hannah's separate follow-up is [CUSTO-10](https://linear.app/pagemantle/issue/CUSTO-10), with the [customer conversation](slack://channel/C7FC302337748032D/message/1790686800.770050) and [account record](hubspot://companies/1aa1f158-4096-512b-8105-606ab20f1be7). The new approval request does not show that this repaired defect returned and does not bypass Policy Gates or audit.
issues.title: Redpoint Assurance: authorize the approved release revision

issues.description:
Ashland Group's site owner excluded a locally varied launch page from a proposed Mantle Kit update, but the page still appeared in the Change Set target list. This affects the proposed preview. No live page change was reported.

Sofia traced the saved exclusion on September 10. The selector included the page before constructing the comparison, so an old comparison snapshot was not the first wrong output. The September 11 restricted change omitted the excluded page while keeping an eligible page selected.

Megan's September 18 review requested more explicit coverage of the other eligible kit consumers before accepting the repair. The first case already retained an eligible page. Identify which consumers or local variants that case did not cover, then extend the selector regression for those gaps. Show which variant carries the exclusion and which eligible consumers remain selected. Repeating the same preview without exposing its coverage would not answer the review.

Sofia extended the regression for older proposal ASH-KIT-P1 on September 22. Megan reviewed and accepted the patch and those tests on September 23. The [Ashland proposal selector report](https://www.notion.so/b87c58b15e824d4999ada3d9cbf4b615) records the tested consumers, exclusion and selected variants. Completion here applies to that tested proposal. It does not establish that every later saved proposal or customer preview is correct.

The later saved proposal ASH-KIT-P2 and its October 1 preview are in the same report. Its current membership check is tracked separately in [ENGIN-19](https://linear.app/pagemantle/issue/ENGIN-19). Camille still needs Ashland Group to confirm the corrected preview for that same proposal. There is no report of a live page change.
issues.title: Ashland Group: honor local-page exclusions in kit targets

issues.description:
Ada confirmed that Publish completed for Redpoint Assurance's original approved release after the ENGIN-16 repair. Her later edited release has changed contents and is labeled rev-later-draft in the redacted case record. Publish is unavailable for that release because it needs new named approval. The labels are case references, not production revision IDs.

Hannah should confirm which changed contents Ada wants to release, route that exact release to its named reviewer, and ask Ada to verify Publish after approval. Lea owns the account follow-up. Keep Policy Gates and audit in place. Do not treat approval of rev-approved as approval of changed contents. See [ENGIN-16](https://linear.app/pagemantle/issue/ENGIN-16) and the [Redpoint customer conversation](slack://channel/C7FC302337748032D/message/1790686800.770050).
issues.title: Redpoint Assurance: obtain approval for edited release

issues.description:
Ashland Group's later saved Mantle Kit proposal ASH-KIT-P2 has an October 1 proposed preview whose target count passes. The actual target membership still needs review against that proposal's page variants and explicit exclusions. The [selector report](https://www.notion.so/b87c58b15e824d4999ada3d9cbf4b615) keeps the raw consumers, exclusions and observed preview targets together. These labels are case references, not production page IDs.

Sofia should compare the expected and observed members for this same proposal, add a regression covering the difference, and send corrected work for review. Camille should then ask Ashland Group's site owner to confirm the corrected preview for ASH-KIT-P2. Completed [ENGIN-5](https://linear.app/pagemantle/issue/ENGIN-5) covers the older tested proposal, not this customer outcome. No live page change has been reported.
issues.title: Ashland Group: check current kit preview targets
